evidence: Independent 275 integer normal-fan combinations with all exterior turns in (0,pi), strict pair eligibility and star classification.
The normal-fan proof applies to arbitrary convex quadrilaterals and any positive integer multiplicity, with finite tests as corroboration only.
correctness.rationale: At every genuine convex quadrilateral vertex, illuminating directions satisfy two strict adjacent outward-normal inequalities. Since each exterior turn lies strictly between zero and pi, no direction can illuminate opposite vertices or three vertices. Adjacent vertex pair i,i+1 is simultaneously illuminated precisely when the two consecutive exterior turns sum to less than pi. Opposite candidate-pair inequalities cannot both hold because the four turns sum to 2pi. Thus admissible pairs form a star; if none, all neighboring turn sums equal pi and the polygon is a parallelogram. One direction therefore hits at most one of the three non-star vertices, giving lower bound 3m (or fractional weight 3), and the witness pair plus individual remaining directions gives 3m; a parallelogram needs 4m. Counting equalities forces the claimed rigidity of every optimum. Independent enumeration checked star/no-disjoint-pair predicates for 275 valid integer normal fans; the argument itself covers arbitrary real turns and m.
risks: Requires four distinct genuine convex vertices; normal-fan star fails in general for polygons with five or more vertices.
